pr_body:
WinUI/XAML requires the `SelectedItem` to be member of the list of
`ItemsSource`. `CascadiaSettings::DefaultTerminals()` is such an `ItemsSource`
and is called every time the launch settings page is visited.
It calls `DefaultTerminal::Available()` which in turn calls `Refresh()`.
While the `SelectedItem` was cached in `CascadiaSettings`, the value of
`DefaultTerminals()` wasn't. Thus every time the page was visited, it refreshed
the `ItemsSource` list without invalidating the current `SelectedItem`.

This commit prevents such accidental mishaps from occurring in the future,
by moving the responsibility of caching solely to the `CascadiaSettings` class.

## PR Checklist
* [x] Closes #11424
* [x] I work here
* [x] Tests added/passed

## Validation Steps Performed
* Navigating between SUI pages maintains the current dropdown selection ✔️
* Saving the settings saves the correct terminal at `HKCU:\Console\%%Startup` ✔️

comments: This _might_ only be applicable with #11397 merged. I'm gonna assign @lhecker for 1.12 to make sure it's not a regression from `main`

review_comments: you can't resist a good cleanup eh :wink: (this is not a bad thing, I just think it is funny)

When I'm opening a file I let clang-tidy run and fix as many issues as is reasonable. And before opening a PR I often try to end up with more lines of code removed than added.

I can stop at any time to be honest, because I know it's a real bother for others (for which I'm very sorry). I'm personally convinced however that it's the right thing to do for a multitude of reasons.
I have no problem with cleanup happening as we go.

I feel like you should set a cleanup item to walk the entire solution to replace `fmt::format` with `fmt::format_to` as I bet we could be using the buffer and format_to way more often for better perf and memory usage.

Maybe it's also interesting to read the reason I do this:
`fmt::format` works by calling (in simplified terms) `fmt::format_to` with a `fmt::memory_buffer` and then constructing a `std::string` using the `memory_buffer`'s `data()` and `size()`. We then in turn construct a `winrt::hstring` from that, which is a bit redundant.
It's still scary binding to a local of qualification `const&` even though I know the compiler "does the right thing"

I know what you might be thinking... "Create a ticket".
But to be honest I personally wouldn't want to ever fix this issue myself, because it works fine the way it is right now... I just wrote it, to explain why it's safe (thanks to `DefaultTerminal::Available()`).
If we're not going to do it, might as well not say "it would be worthwhile". :smile:
